title: Project 8: modular multi-file C application
learningObjectives: Explain the topic and its C rules.
Trace the example and identify its purpose.
Identify important validation and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a tested program or reference exercise.

understand.concept: A modular C application separates public declarations, implementation files, application entry points and tests. Each module should expose a small interface and keep implementation details private where possible.
understand.whyItMatters: Modular organization supports maintainability, independent testing and team collaboration as a C program grows.
understand.analogy: Treat the project or language feature as a set of components with explicit interfaces and responsibilities.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal language, library and resource-management rules.

explain.narrative:
A modular C application separates public declarations, implementation files, application entry points and tests. Each module should expose a small interface and keep implementation details private where possible.

For a complete implementation, define input constraints, ownership, error handling and test cases before coding. Compile with warnings and verify normal, boundary and failure behaviour.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The header declares the public function and the source file defines it. A build command compiles and links both source files; a real project should add tests and error contracts.

practise.guidedTask: Identify public interface versus implementation detail.
practise.independentTask: Create a three-module program with headers, source files, a Makefile and a test plan.
hints: Avoid exposing mutable internal state unnecessarily.
Ensure every external function has one compatible declaration and one definition.
